what: A single droplet path endlessly morphs between preset shapes, taking 10 seconds per shape with easeInOutQuad, and sways slowly. Put the path inside a clipPath and the shape of the hero video · photo window changes as if breathing (Snap.svg 0.5.1 animate, chaining the next shape each time one ends).

options.dur: Length of one cycle (seconds), default 10 — 0 is not accepted (the ring would spin endlessly within a single frame)
options.ease: linear makes it straight (default is easeInOutQuad)
options.[data-fx-part=path]: Morphing path (child, one) — the initial d is the first shape. May be placed inside a clipPath
options.[data-fx-part=form]: Paths of the following shapes (children, one or more) — only d is read, nothing is drawn. Even if node counts differ, Snap interpolates them as curves

use: <svg data-fx="snap-path-morph" data-fx-snap-path-morph="dur: 10" width="0" height="0"><defs><clipPath id="win" clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox"><path data-fx-part="path" d="M.5 0C.8 0 1 .3 1 .5S.8 1 .5 1 0 .7 0 .5.2 0 .5 0Z"/></clipPath><path data-fx-part="form" d="…"/><path data-fx-part="form" d="…"/></defs></svg> — style on the window element="clip-path: url(#win)"
note: Load ../_vendor/snapsvg@0.5.1/snap.svg-min.js first. The original-shaped path data is not carried over, the consuming side supplies its own shapes

from.where: index.js hero water-drop window (.td-hfv clipPath) — original Snap("#svg-morphing-mv_pc") path animate(10000ms, mina.easeInOutQuad) is chained to the next shape each time it ends. The site cycles our five seed droplet shapes with the same Snap.svg 0.5.1
